title: Ground-field retagging preserves the full tower purity comparison
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0$ of characteristic $p$, an algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with ring of integers $\mathcal O_E$, and put $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\ell^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-pur-conventions, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes with structural maps $a_X,a_Y$, and let $f:X\to Y$ be a smooth separated $k$-morphism of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $\sigma:k\simeq k$ fix $k_0$, and write $T^{\langle\sigma\rangle}$ for the same underlying scheme $T$ with structural map $\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma)\circ a_T$, for $T=X,Y$, and $f^{\langle\sigma\rangle}$ for the same underlying morphism between these retagged schemes.

Use the ordinary derived categories of varying-coefficient strict towers [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers] and their uniformly bounded constructible finite-Tor subcategories [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers], with the tower adjunctions $F_f=Rf_{!,\bullet}\dashv G_f=f^!_\bullet$ of [det-sp-tower-gluing], and the natural purity maps $\gamma_{f,\bullet}(K_\bullet):f_\bullet^*K_\bullet(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\sim}G_fK_\bullet$ of [det-sp-tower-gamma]. The tensor products and twists in this construction are ordinary tower tensor products and the levelwise Tate twists [def-weil-derived-tensor, def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Identify the small pro-etale sites and coefficient systems by the identity of underlying schemes, identify $F_f$ and $F_{f^{\langle\sigma\rangle}}$ using the same underlying compactification, and identify their right adjoints by the unique counit-preserving adjunction isomorphism. Then for every $K_\bullet$ in the indicated constructible finite-Tor category, under these identifications of sources and targets,
$$\gamma_{f^{\langle\sigma\rangle},\bullet}(K_\bullet)=\gamma_{f,\bullet}(K_\bullet)$$
as an equality of morphisms in the ordinary derived category of towers, retaining the quotient-coefficient transitions. No normalization of $K_\bullet$ is required.

source.place: Steps 1–3 on coefficient towers; invariance of the tensor-map transpose under ground-field retagging (explicit auxiliary comparison)

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-tower-operations-ground-field-retagging] to identify the ordinary derived tower categories, pullbacks, tensor constraints, Tate twists and same-compactification compact-support functor. These identifications retain the actual quotient transitions and identify the uniformly bounded constructible finite-Tor domains. Write $\rho:G_{f^{\langle\sigma\rangle}}\xrightarrow{\sim}G_f$ for the stipulated counit-preserving identification.

source.place: Step 1, tower purity comparison under the identity of underlying sites and compactification

proof.text: By [lem-pur-orientation-ground-field-retagging], the normalized orientations satisfy $\rho_{\mathbf1}\circ a_{f^{\langle\sigma\rangle},\bullet}=a_{f,\bullet}$ in the ordinary tower derived category, with quotient transitions retained.

source.place: Step 1, normalized tower orientation under ground-field retagging

proof.text: For every $K_\bullet$ in the stated category, [lem-pur-tower-tensor-transpose-ground-field-retagging] gives $\rho_K\circ t^{\mathrm{retag}}_K=t_{f,K}\circ(1\otimes\rho_{\mathbf1})$. By [det-sp-tower-gamma](2), $\gamma$ is the common twist reassociation followed by $1\otimes a$ and $t$. Substitute the equality of Step 2 in this formula: $\rho_K\circ\gamma_{f^{\langle\sigma\rangle},\bullet}(K_\bullet)=t_{f,K}\circ(1\otimes\rho_{\mathbf1})\circ(1\otimes a_{\mathrm{retag}})\circ\mathrm{reassoc}=t_{f,K}\circ(1\otimes a_f)\circ\mathrm{reassoc}=\gamma_{f,\bullet}(K_\bullet)$. This is the claimed equality under the identifications. Every cited assertion applies to all uniformly bounded constructible finite-Tor towers, so normalization is unnecessary.

Re-split note (2026-10-21): no argument of the old proof is lost. Old Step 1 (same sites, towers, twists via u^{l^r}=1, same compactification) became the operations node, stated in more detail. Old Step 2 is still the orientation lemma (rho_1 a_retag = a_f). Old Step 3 became the transpose node: the claim that PF is the same transformation, the naturality in the omega slot, eps_f F(rho)=eps_retag, equal transposes and injectivity of the gluing Hom bijection. The item proof is a 3-step assembly of about 1.4k characters; the new nodes are about 2.1k and 2.6k characters, so of comparable size, and neither restates the item. Maths checked: C_K F(1⊗rho_1)=C_K^sigma, then the transposes agree by the gluing bijection on C_X. Step 3 substitution: rho_K gamma^sigma = t(1⊗rho_1)(1⊗a^sigma)reassoc = gamma_f, which is genuinely elementary. Each construction depends only on the underlying schemes and the site, so the operations node is true. Small cases checked: sigma=id, f=id with d=0, empty X, K=0, ramified E (A_n=A_{E,en}), and non-normalized towers. B1-B3 hold: both new nodes have empty proofs, and their bracketed citations equal their stmt_deps. No SGA source is used. grep for 'retag' over the DAG finds no duplicate statement.
